chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: Neal Hefti and The Atomic Basie
summary: They discuss Hefti's arrangements as a formula that arrangers imitated.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now, another theory of mine is that when you make that album with Neal Hefti's arrangements, 'The Atomic Basie'.
Mm hmm.
That's a very big success. And, from that time on, most of the arrangers have been more or less doing imitations of Neal Hefti.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
You know, you listen to these newer albums, they --
Mm hmm.
mostly seem to be listening to what Neal Hefti did.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
You know there're things sort of like 'Lil' Darling'.
Yeah. Yeah.
I mean, that must have been a very big influence on them. I mean, after all, you're still playing some of that style.
Yeah. We still do some of those things, and I don't know -- I think that has alot to do with it -- Neal's arrangements -- as far as the band is concerned, and as far as the arrangers.
Yeah.
I guess they're probably sticking close to that format, more or less, you know. But, I think it came around to a change during that period with Marshall.
Yeah. Well, it seems to me that Marshall and Neal Hefti's arrangements -- the success of those two together --
Mm hmm.
-- sort of really made a kind of formula?
Mm hmm. Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
A commercial formula, you mean?
Well, I mean, it's very popular.
Yes. Yes. Mm hmm.
This is where this, you know, this new sense of dynamics, you know -- where it's very soft --
Mm hmm. Mm hmm. Yeah.
-- then [—]
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
But, I mean, certainly the two albums that Benny Carter did and the one that Quincy Jones did --
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
-- you know -- before you --
Mm hmm.
-- they were different, and I thought they were very good.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
And, then we have to also mention in this period the impact of Joe Williams and "Every Day",.
That's right. And, you have to -- now, what year are we --
Well, that's just it. We're getting too far ahead again.
Excuse me. Yeah.
